title: Technology and its impact
subtitle: wi-fi, biotechnology, techie, trackpad
summary: Name the technologies that shape daily life - digital, wi-fi, satellite, biotechnology, AI, ergonomics - and the devices and screen words that go with them.

lesson.heading: Technological advances affecting daily life
rows: digital photography, digital video and audio recording, digital broadcasting
a system for connecting electronic devices to the internet without using wires
genetic modification of plants, for example disease-resistant crops
design of environments so people can work efficiently and comfortably
connecting electronic devices to each other with no wires

lesson.heading: These technologies in sentences
lesson.text: Notice the key words that travel with each technology: **analogue** is the opposite of **digital**; **GPS** stands for global positioning system; a crop that resists disease is **disease-resistant**.

examples.text: The sound quality of a **digital** voice recorder is superior to that of an **analogue** one.
The hotel has **wi-fi** in every room.
She doesn't use a road map now because her new car has **GPS** built in, so she gave me her old plug-in **SATNAV**.
**Biotechnology** companies are experimenting with new, **disease-resistant** crops for farmers.

lesson.heading: AI, ergonomics and Bluetooth
lesson.text: Scientists working in **artificial intelligence** want computers to work more like the human brain. **Ergonomically designed** furniture is designed to give maximum comfort and efficiency. **Bluetooth** connects one device to another without wires.

examples.text: Scientists working in **AI** are hoping to create computers that will be more and more like the human brain.
My car has **Bluetooth**, so I can connect my phone to the speakers.

lesson.heading: Devices a techie owns
rows: a mobile phone that can be used as a small computer
an earpiece and microphone so you can use a mobile without holding it
a card for entering your workplace or college
a small portable computer with a screen, keyboard and trackpad
a computer that stays on a table at home or in the office
a thin computer using a touchscreen, such as an iPad
a device for reading books, such as a Kindle
a TV you can send comments to while watching a programme
a device that lets you connect to the internet from different devices
lesson.note: A techie is a person who loves acquiring all the new technology - a positive, friendly word.

lesson.heading: Words for what is on the screen
lesson.text: A **thumbnail** is a small picture you click on to see the full-size version. An **icon** is a small symbol representing a program. A **screensaver** is the image that appears if you do not use the computer for a while. An **app**, short for application, is a piece of special software. A **trackpad** is the flat area on a laptop you use instead of a mouse, and a machine's **footprint** is the amount of desk space it takes up.

examples.text: Just click on that **icon** there to open the program.
I've downloaded a great new gaming **app** onto my phone.
This new printer's got a smaller **footprint** than the one I had before.

left.label: techie
left.text: Someone who loves getting all the newest technology. The word has no negative associations.
examples: I'm a bit of a **techie** really; I love getting the latest mobile phone or digital camera.

right.label: computer nerd
right.text: A rather negative term for someone obsessed with computers, who devotes most of their time to them at the expense of a normal social life.
examples: My younger brother's a real **computer nerd**. He never goes out, and all he ever thinks about is computers.

lesson.heading: technical, technological, technique
lesson.text: **Technical** (adverb **technically**) relates to the knowledge, machines and materials used in science and industry. **Technological** (adverb **technologically**) relates to technology itself. Only **technically** can also mean 'according to an exact understanding of the facts'. A **technician** is a skilled worker who looks after equipment, and a **technique** is a particular way of doing something.

examples.text: Removing the salt from sea water is a **technically** complex process.
**Technologically**, their company is a long way behind ours.
The recession is **technically** over but things are still difficult for many people.
Andrea has a very interesting **technique** for remembering vocabulary.

lesson.text: Call someone a techie and you are being friendly; call them a computer nerd and you are not.

exercises.prompt: Which type of technology would you associate with each person or thing?

pairs.left: a yachtswoman establishing her exact position
a designer making a more comfortable keyboard
a scientist producing wheat that resists insects
a camera whose photos you store on your phone
a computer that can make decisions for itself
a car music player your phone connects to with no wires

exercises.prompt: 'I prefer it to my mobile because it's bigger but still light enough to carry. I can Skype on it and take photos with it, but I can't make ordinary phone calls.' What is the speaker describing?
exercises.explanation: A tablet is a thin touchscreen computer such as an iPad.

exercises.prompt: 'I changed its position and now I can get online from any room in the house.' What is it?
exercises.explanation: A router lets you connect to the internet from different devices around the house.

exercises.prompt: You can look at ___ pictures on the website and then click on them to see the full-size version.
exercises.explanation: A thumbnail is a small picture you click on to see the full-size version.

exercises.prompt: My younger brother's a real computer ___ . He never goes out, and all he ever thinks about is computers.
exercises.explanation: Computer nerd is negative: someone obsessed with computers at the expense of a normal social life.

exercises.prompt: I'm a bit of a ___ really; I love getting the latest mobile phone or digital camera.
exercises.explanation: Techie has none of the negative associations that nerd has.

exercises.prompt: I've downloaded a great new gaming ___ onto my phone.
exercises.explanation: An app is a piece of special software; the word is short for application.

exercises.prompt: His ___ on his laptop is a really cool picture of the night sky.
exercises.hint: (what appears when you stop using the computer)
exercises.explanation: A screensaver is the image that appears if the computer is not used for a while.

exercises.prompt: Just click on that ___ there to open the program.
exercises.explanation: An icon is a small symbol representing a program.

exercises.prompt: I don't really like this ___ on my laptop; I'd prefer a proper mouse.
exercises.explanation: A trackpad is the flat area on a laptop used instead of a mouse.

exercises.prompt: Karl got a good job as a lab ___ in the university.
exercises.hint: (techn... : a skilled worker who looks after equipment)
exercises.explanation: A technician is a skilled person who looks after scientific or industrial equipment.

exercises.statement: In this country, young people technologically become adults at the age of 18.
exercises.explanation: The word here is technically: in this country, young people technically become adults at the age of 18. Technically can mean 'according to an exact understanding of the facts'; technologically cannot.
